feature.label: Old Sevier
feature.title: Pitch a Friend is back at Hi-Wire Friday night: put your single friend on a slideshow and make the case to a room full of strangers
feature.deck: Free, and the presenters drink free too.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Fri Nov 20 · 7 PM · the Single Mingle Mixer after the pitches

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Hi-Wire Brewing · 2020 Barber St, second floor · the taproom is open 3 – 11

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Free to attend · pitch spots are limited, sign up ahead through the brewery's link in bio · presenters get a free drink

facts.label: How it works
facts.value: Short, lighthearted presentations about why your friend is great, what they want, and why someone in the room should ask them out

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: Mostly sunny and 68, down to 38 overnight · it is all indoors

body.text: Hi-Wire runs the neighborhood's oddest dating night again on Friday, and it costs nothing to watch. Pitch a Friend is exactly what it sounds like: you have a single friend you know deserves to be somebody's next crush, so you sign them up, build a few slides and stand up in a taproom to make the case. The brewery's description of the format is online dating with your friends doing the matchmaking, and a lot more fun. The pitches are short and meant to be funny, covering who the friend is, what they are looking for and why someone in the room should probably ask them out.
The rules of the room

Pitch spots are limited and go by sign-up through the brewery's link in bio, and every presenter gets a complimentary drink for their trouble. Nobody has to pitch to come. Once the slideshows wrap, Hi-Wire keeps the room going with what it calls a Single Mingle Mixer, so the people who just got pitched and the people who watched can actually talk. It starts at seven on the brewery's second floor on Barber Street, and the whole thing is free. Friday is mostly sunny and 68 on the way in and 38 by closing, which is a good argument for the indoor decks.

body.text: Four birthdays land in one week at Fly by Night, the seventies cocktail lounge on Sevier Avenue, so the bar is making a race of it. Thursday at nine it is the Super Birthday gran prix, celebrating, in the bar's words, your favorite club racers as they speed around the sun: Jocelyn Morin, the silversmith who owns Fly by Night and Tern Club, and the DJs Benicio, Minitiger and Tiny, who between them run most of the lounge's dance nights. body.text: Visualize Art Studio, the glass-teaching studio out west on Center Park Drive, brings its mobile stained glass workshop to Hi-Wire's taproom on Sunday at three. The format is the studio's two-hour intro: you start with a pre-cut, pre-ground kit of glass in one of three November designs, a pumpkin, a cowboy boot or a bat, pick your colors, and learn to copper-foil and solder the pieces into a finished panel you take home. No experience is expected, everything is supplied, and the ticket is eighty dollars through the studio's site. The same studio runs hot-glass and stained-glass sessions at Ijams Nature Center on Saturday morning, if Sunday does not suit.

body.text: Ijams Nature Center has a new animal ambassador, and it is an opossum. Playing 'Possum, Saturday at one, is the park's hour-long introduction: a naturalist presents the animal and makes the case for the misunderstood marsupial, which eats ticks, plays dead on purpose and carries its young in a pouch, and then the group learns the basics of nature journaling and draws its own opossum to take home. It is built for ages five and up, ten dollars a person, and the page says the program sits mostly in one place, so small kids are fine. Register ahead; there are no walk-ins at Ijams programs.

body.text: Cyanotype is the old blueprint process: paper coated with a UV-reacting solution, something laid on it, sunlight, and a white silhouette on Prussian blue. Saturday at 2:30 an Ijams naturalist walks a beginners' class through it. You forage your own leaves and seed heads around the visitor center, arrange them, expose the paper in the sun and rinse, and go home with several prints and the recipe to do it again. Eighteen dollars, ages fourteen and up, mostly indoors with the short walk out to gather. The forecast is mostly sunny, which for this class is the whole lesson plan.

body.text: The park's meditative morning, moved from the first of the month to this Sunday, runs ten to noon at the Homesite, the old Ijams family grounds up the hill from the visitor center. It goes in three movements: an outdoor yoga flow to start, a sound bath in the pavilion, and a forest-bathing session to finish, which is the slow, unhurried kind of walk in the trees that the Japanese call shinrin-yoku. The park's pitch is the research, lower stress and better focus, and the ticket is forty dollars with pre-registration required. Bring a mat; the morning starts at 41 degrees and climbs toward 67, so the first pose is the cold one.

body.text: Moss rocks, says the park, and Sunday afternoon it spends two hours proving it. The Moss Meander meets at the picnic tables in the Mead's Quarry lot at one and wanders the quarry's rocks and shaded banks with an Ijams naturalist, learning to tell the species apart and what each one is doing for the forest around it. The park's own pitch starts with the fairy stuff from childhood and ends with moss as the organism that holds the story of the forest in its structure. Fifteen dollars, sixteen and up, and a sunny 67-degree November afternoon at the quarry is about as good as the setting gets.

body.text: Earl's, the bar and kitchen on Waterfront Drive at Suttree Landing, runs one special a day from eleven to ten, and Saturday the game-day specials go on top of it. The Vols host LSU at Neyland at 3:30, which puts the stadium crowd on the bridges all afternoon and the game on every screen on this side of the river. Earl's game-day list is the same every Saturday: two dollars off drafts, six-dollar Orange Bliss cocktails, six beer buckets for the price of five, two dollars off pizza and four- and five-dollar shots all day, with eight-dollar house margaritas as the standing Saturday deal. Thursday is ten-dollar Patrón mango ritas, Friday nine-dollar spicy pineapple ritas, and Sunday seven-dollar mimosas and Bloody Marys, all four afternoons sunny and in the upper sixties.

Up on Sevier, Printshop takes a dollar off pints from half an hour before kickoff until the final whistle, Kern's puts the game on its big screens every Saturday, and SouthSide Garage, which has posted a five-dollar Vol Bomb for every game this month, is open noon to midnight.
